svg.title: Apache Flink
svg.desc: Apache Flink. A stream processor: stateful operators over unbounded streams, with event time, windows and exactly-once checkpoints. Step 1, Where it sits: Flink reads orders from Kafka, keeps a count per card, writes fraud alerts and per-minute counts. Step 2, Dataflow and keyed state: keyBy(card) sends all of C-9's orders to count 3/3; the sixth, made at 10:07, makes 6 > 5: an alert. Step 3, Event time and watermarks: Watermark: latest event time − 5 s. At 10:10 the [10:00, 10:10) windows close; late orders go aside. Step 4, Checkpoints and the limits: Every 30 s barriers snapshot state and offsets to S3; after a crash Flink resumes from chk 812.

g.text: Flink reads orders from Kafka, keeps a count per card, writes fraud alerts and per-minute counts.
keyBy(card) sends all of C-9's orders to count 3/3; the sixth, made at 10:07, makes 6 > 5: an alert.
Watermark: latest event time − 5 s. At 10:10 the [10:00, 10:10) windows close; late orders go aside.
Every 30 s barriers snapshot state and offsets to S3; after a crash Flink resumes from chk 812.
state lives here: RocksDB on local disk
Flink reads every order from Kafka as it arrives, keeps state about what it has seen, and keeps writing alerts and per-minute counts.
It runs as one long-lived job on a cluster: Kubernetes here, or a managed service such as Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink.
the state lives with the computation, not in a database
Each source subtask reads one partition. keyBy(card) hashes C-9 to key group 126 of 128, owned by count 3/3, so all its orders meet there.
Keyed state counts C-9’s orders in [10:00, 10:10). The sixth, made at 10:07, makes 6 > 5 and an alert goes to fraud-alerts.
Barriers from the sources make each operator snapshot its state, with the Kafka offsets, to S3. After the crash the job resumes from chk 812.
W = largest event time seen − 5 s
a window closes once W passes its end
